title: 5 Best Databricks Frontend Builders in 2026
summary: Five ways to put a frontend on Databricks lakehouse data, from Databricks' own apps and dashboards to no-code tools for business teams.
body_markdown:
Databricks holds more and more of the data operations teams need: customer usage, supplier performance, cleaned reference tables. Getting that data in front of those teams, in a form they can act on, needs a frontend. Databricks now offers its own options, and there are external tools for people who do not work in the workspace.


Below are five Databricks frontend builders, with the point where each one stops. For SQL clients, see the[best Databricks GUI tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-databricks-gui-tools/) .


## The five options at a glance


Option Builds Viewers need workspace access? Cost


Jet Admin Internal tools, portals and dashboards No Free plan; paid tiers


Databricks Apps Python or JavaScript apps in the workspace Yes Included; compute billed


AI/BI dashboards and Genie Dashboards and natural-language Q&A Yes, with sharing options Included; compute billed


Sigma Spreadsheet-style BI with write-back Sigma users Paid


Retool Developer-built internal tools No Free tier; paid per user


## The options


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to a Databricks SQL warehouse and builds a frontend on your tables: search, record pages, forms, approval steps and dashboards, optionally combined with operational databases and APIs in the same app. You describe the app and Jet generates it, then refine it visually or in code. Data stays in Databricks.


People sign in to the app with no workspace seat, and roles decide which rows and fields each person sees. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** notebooks, pipelines and model work stay in Databricks.


### 2. Databricks Apps


Databricks Apps hosts web apps built with Streamlit, Dash, Flask or Node.js inside your workspace under Unity Catalog governance.


**Where it stops:** every screen is code, and apps use compute while running.


### 3. AI/BI dashboards and Genie


Databricks' AI/BI dashboards and Genie spaces let analysts publish dashboards and let users ask questions in natural language against curated data.


**Where it stops:** they are for reading and asking, not editing records or running processes.


### 4. Sigma


Sigma connects to Databricks with a spreadsheet interface and input tables that write back.


**Where it stops:** it is BI first, not operational screens.


### 5. Retool


Retool connects to Databricks, and developers build internal tools with components and JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** per-user pricing and developer maintenance.


## Which to use


- **Business teams need to act on Databricks data without workspace seats:** Jet Admin.
- **Your data team writes Python apps:** Databricks Apps.
- **Users need dashboards and natural-language questions:** AI/BI and Genie.
- **Analysts want spreadsheet-style BI with write-back:** Sigma.
- **Developers will build internal tools:** Retool.


## Start with who needs the data


Users inside the workspace have Databricks' own tools. Everyone else needs a frontend outside it.[Connect Databricks to Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/databricks) and build one.
